title: Broadway Flea Market & Grand Auction
description: Broadway Cares celebrates the event’s 40th year with more than 60 tables of theatrical collectibles, an autograph and photo area, and live and silent auctions.
venue: Shubert Alley, West 44th and West 45th Streets, and Times Square
price_label: Free to browse; auction and merchandise prices vary
fit_reason: A Broadway-lover’s treasure hunt near Hell’s Kitchen, with memorabilia and performers.

title: 2026 Magical Girls Festival
description: An all-ages convention devoted to magical-girl anime and manga, with screenings, vendors, activities, panels, cosplay, voice actors, and a Madoka Magica anniversary spotlight.
fit_reason: A focused anime-and-manga day with screenings and fan programming at a modest price.

title: Give Us Our Daily Dread: Horror Comics
description: James Tynion IV, Chris Condon, and Ezra Claytan Daniels discuss the continuing growth of horror comics and their recent graphic novels at the Brooklyn Book Festival.
fit_reason: A free panel squarely about comics, graphic novels, and genre storytelling.

title: Fall Into Fantasy
description: Fantasy authors Sarah Beth Durst, Amélie Wen Zhao, and Shannon J. Spann discuss worldbuilding, magic, romance, power, and family in their recent novels.
venue: Brooklyn Law School Student Lounge, 250 Joralemon Street
fit_reason: A free fiction event devoted to imaginative worlds and the craft behind them.

title: When We Gather: On Food, Celebration, and Ritual
description: Brooklyn Book Festival panel with anthropologist Ashanté Reese, entertaining expert Amber Mayfield Hewett, and chef Natasha Pickowicz on gathering over shared food, moderated by Danielle Davenport of BEM.
fit_reason: A free outdoor Festival Day conversation about food and culture, easy to fold into the same trip as the comics and fantasy panels.

title: Game-A-Palooza 2026
description: IGDA NYC’s curated indie-game showcase opens its locally made and unreleased games to the public from 1 PM, with opportunities to play and meet New York developers.
fit_reason: Hands-on access to unreleased games and local developers for only $10.

title: New York Comic Con 2026
description: NYCC’s 20th-anniversary edition spans comics, anime, manga, science fiction, gaming, authors, cosplay, film, television, exhibitors, and creator appearances.
venue: Jacob K. Javits Convention Center, 429 11th Avenue
price_label: Adult single-day Thursday tickets $103.98 including taxes and fees; Saturday, 4-day, and VIP passes sold out
fit_reason: A nearby convention bringing comics, manga, anime, science fiction, and gaming together.

title: Personal Agent Hackathon
description: Cognee’s hands-on collabathon at NYU Tandon for anyone building AI agents: pick a personal use case, add your own data, build a connected memory, and ship an agent that can use it. Lightning talks at 10:45 AM, building from 11 AM, judging at 3:30 PM.
price_label: Free; RSVP required for campus access
fit_reason: A free, hands-on agent-building day that matches his AI-and-programming career goal, with a career-brain and personal-knowledge use case as the example projects.

title: Harlem Run: Monday Night Run
description: Free, inclusive pacer-led runs and walks through Harlem, starting and ending at Marcus Garvey Park. Paces from 7 to 12 minutes per mile plus run/walk and walk groups; open to all ages and abilities, with bag drop available.
venue: Marcus Garvey Park, south side of Pelham Fritz Recreation Center, W 122nd St and Mount Morris Park West
fit_reason: A free weekly group run in Harlem with pacers for every pace - a standing Monday-night habit that costs nothing.

title: The 51st Annual Atlantic Antic
description: A mile-long neighborhood street festival with hundreds of vendors, food, crafts, shopping, live music, entertainment, and family areas along Atlantic Avenue.
venue: Atlantic Avenue from Hicks Street to Fourth Avenue
price_label: Free admission; food and merchandise vary
fit_reason: A big food-and-culture street festival with live music and plenty to browse.

title: Día de los Muertos at NYBG
description: A monthlong celebration of memory, life, and renewal featuring marigold displays, a community ofrenda, calaveras, a flower-covered Catrina, weekend music and crafts, and special performances.
venue: New York Botanical Garden, 2900 Southern Boulevard
fit_reason: A substantial cultural celebration in the Bronx with botanical displays, art, music, crafts, and community traditions.

title: Fall for Dance Festival
description: The 23rd Fall for Dance Festival brings 15 companies and 11 premieres to New York City Center across five programs, including A.I.M by Kyle Abraham, The Royal Ballet, San Francisco Ballet, Boston Ballet, and two City Center commissions. Remaining programs run September 26 through October 3.
price_label: $30 all seats; free pre-show dance lesson for ticketholders
fit_reason: World-class dance for $30 a seat a short walk from Hell's Kitchen, with a free pre-show class for ticketholders.

title: Brooklyn Book Festival Festival Day
description: The festival's flagship day fills Brooklyn Borough Hall and the surrounding venues and parks with author panels and a literary marketplace, with Marlon James, Colson Whitehead, Tracy K. Smith, Douglas Stuart, Cristina Rivera Garza, and dozens more.
venue: Brooklyn Borough Hall and surrounding venues
fit_reason: A free all-day book festival, with the comics and genre panels he follows alongside the big literary names.

title: NYC Off-Broadway Week
description: NYC Tourism's biannual Off-Broadway promotion returns with 2-for-1 tickets, 50% off each seat, to participating Off-Broadway productions across the city; the lineup of shows goes live September 22.
price_label: 2-for-1 tickets (50% off); service fee applied per ticket
fit_reason: The cheapest reliable route into Off-Broadway all year: 2-for-1 seats, with the participating shows announced September 22.

title: Queer in Every Career: LGBTQ+ Career Fair 2026
description: The Center’s annual career fair connects LGBTQ+ job seekers with affirming NYC employers, networking, resume feedback, coaching, and skill-building workshops.
venue: The Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual & Transgender Community Center, 208 W 13th Street
fit_reason: A queer community event with practical career-change support, workshops, and networking.

title: Horror and Dark Literature Book Club: The October Country
description: An in-person adult discussion of Ray Bradbury’s The October Country, focused on horror and dark literature.
fit_reason: A free adult book-club night for horror, dark fantasy, and classic science fiction readers.
